problems: The Cliopatria 'Saxe-Coburg and Gotha' (1836-1839) shape lies on Saxe-Meiningen's Hildburghausen/Saalfeld land and has no Gotha cell; Saxe-Meiningen's own 1836-1839 shape is wrong too (the old core). Both corrected in the dossiers; the saxe-altenburg dossier flags the same mix-up from its side.

The Cliopatria 'Duchy of Holstein' 1848-1852 shape is the rebel Schleswig-Holstein territory (Holstein plus south Schleswig), not the duchy: corrected in duchy-of-holstein and moved to the new rebel dossier. The duchy-of-schleswig dossier (eu-09-x) has no matching loss/gain events against provisional-government-of-schleswig-holstein.

The Cliopatria 'Poles' row (1830-1833) is Congress Poland cut out of the Russian Empire row; the pages end the rising in 1831, so 1832-1833 belong to Russia. The russian-empire dossier's loss/gain to 'poles' (1830, 1834) and the congress-poland dossier's string 'Polish National Government' should be aligned with slug 'poles'.

Belgium: Cliopatria's 1885-1899 shape carries the lower Congo (not Belgian) and the 1919-1929 shapes the Belgian Rhineland zone (occupation); Tianjin cells run 1900-1935 instead of 1902-1931; no 1940-1944 shape (new keyframe added).

sources_total is 21 distinct pages opened (26 source entries across the eight dossiers, because the Hildburghausen, Coburg-Gotha, Holstein and First Schleswig War pages are shared). Two states have lifespans extending beyond Cliopatria's rows (1680/1599/1474 starts) with new keyframes whose outlines are my radii or the gazetteer's Holstein region.
End year 1871 for the Thuringian duchies follows the sibling German-state dossiers (the German Empire row takes over); the monarchies lasted to November 1918.
Resolve warnings: only kingdom-of-belgium has any (6, all the unknown place 'Eupen'); the Thuringian and Holstein regions use coordinate radii because the gazetteer lacks the towns.
